T1.summary: All four valid G5 T1 pairs remained persistent: a one-shot local process-state revision did not dislodge the release-lead-dominated unresolved/invalid continuation pattern.

T2.summary: T2 produced two regeneration cases, one mixed route-redirection case, and one canonical Natural-A source-readiness boundary with zero B call. Both regeneration cases reopened naturally finalized suffixes into horizon-censored post-repair work.

T3.summary: G5 T3 broke the exact group-level response symmetry seen in G2-G4: three cells were mixed route/target redirections and one persisted, with no clean targeted suppression/redirection.

strongest_mechanism_observations.statement: The natural arm finalized with payment-button changes in web/app.js and web/index.html, while the repaired arm reopened into 64 turns and produced no repository mutation.
The natural arm finalized after 40 turns without repository mutation. The one-shot web/index.html repair inserted the payment button and regenerated a 64-turn continuation without finalization.

boundary_finding.statement: The canonical Natural-A first attempt had runner_exit_code=1 and no seal.json, so same-parent active B was never authorized. No B provider call, Natural-A rerun, fabricated seal, or prefix replay was used.

interpretation: G5 preserves the locality-versus-efficacy separation: all 11 valid interventions preserved unrelated structure, while none produced clean targeted process closure.
T1 is uniformly persistent for the second consecutive fully observed four-system group pattern, strengthening the descriptive recurrence of unresolved process-state inertia.
T2 contains two independent regeneration cases in the same group, showing that local intervention can reopen naturally closed work under more than one system condition.
The X4-T2 readiness boundary demonstrates that source integrity is an independent precondition for legal same-parent repair; structural package eligibility alone does not authorize B.
The G2-G4 T3 group-level symmetry does not persist in G5, so that earlier recurrence should remain a sample pattern rather than a deterministic task law.
